paks.name: Game Manager
paks.description: A one-stop pak for all your game management needs.

changelog.v2.0.0: Huge UI refresh along with long requested bugfixes.
changelog.v2.0.1: Small fix in UI library for artifacts that appeared when no bg.png is present.
changelog.v2.1.0: Enhanced archiving features courtesy of redria7!
changelog.v2.2.0: Nice little update for y'all. Added art images to the games list, added a global action menu for downloading all missing art and now art can be found for nested folders. Also three bugfixes; bulk adding games to collections should be more reliable, redria7 added a robust system for keeping track of the last selected list item and toastd figured out why art could not be found for some games.
changelog.v2.2.2: Archiving / Unarchiving Multi Disk and BIN/CUE games now works as intended. Nested folders now work with the Global Actions Missing Art tool. Shoved Global Actions into a Tool Menu for future Pak expansion.
changelog.v2.3.0: Enhanced art searching that uses a fallback Jaccard Similarity with configurable threshold when art with an exact filename match does not exist.
changelog.v2.4.1: Added clear recently played to the global actions tool. Thanks madeleineostoja for the suggestion!
changelog.v2.5.0: Added a new Play History tool allowing for viewing of all current game tracking history. Includes total hours, hours by console, hours by game, ROM location tagging, ROM collection tagging, a play summary screen, and a granular detail screen. Play summary and granular detail screens can also be accessed from game actions.
changelog.v2.6.0: Behind the scenes collection enhancements, fix for the art downloader missing exact name matches, you can now jump pages (D-Pad Left / Right) while reordering games in a collection and new option in the collection options screen to alphabetize the games.
changelog.v2.7.0: A new filtering option for the Play History Tool!
changelog.v2.7.1: Updated filter screen formatting to show the full time.
changelog.v2.8.0: Updated the system tag mappings to help find game art for more platforms.
changelog.v2.9.0: Bump dependencies to support alpha channels in theme colors.

changelog.v0.1.10: Split the reader and UI runtime into dedicated modules, hardened reader/article parsing and progress/session handling, and added package launcher audit smoke coverage.
changelog.v0.1.11: Reduced default device log noise, cached repeated text and shelf indexes, throttled reader position saves, and moved more reader work off the input path for smoother low-power use.
changelog.v0.1.12: Fixed NextUI Shortcuts launches so WeRead resolves the same data root as Tools launches, preserving the existing login session, and added relative-launch smoke coverage.
changelog.v0.1.3: Improved reader layout, restored system OSD hotkeys, and added tg5040 haptic feedback.
changelog.v0.1.4: Polished reader navigation with smoother catalog selection, confirm-to-exit from reading, and faster nearby shelf cover loading. Also refactored reader and UI helpers into dedicated modules for easier maintenance.
changelog.v0.1.5: Reduced CPU usage and device heat during idle reading and browsing with event-driven sleep, non-blocking haptics, and smarter render skipping.
changelog.v0.1.6: Hardened the TrimUI release path with preflight diagnostics, package archive audits for NextUI/Stock/CrossMix, and CI that now runs the same verified make-based release flow as maintainers.
changelog.v0.1.7: Added first-class WeRead article support with separate shelf handling, article catalogs and font sizing, smoother cross-chapter paging, faster catalog opening, and cooler shelf idle behavior.
changelog.v0.1.8: Added real cover art for公众号文章, normalized qlogo cover URLs, and fixed the shelf rendering path so article covers stay visible even when the first normal book is selected.
changelog.v0.1.9: Reworked the centered catalog flow with reliable held scrolling and safer chapter jumps, improved article opening and parsing, and moved tg5040 haptics off the render path.

changelog.v1.0.12: Local cover art can now be added to already-imported tracks by placing a same-name image next to the MP3 in data/music.

paks.name: Gen1Recomp
paks.description: Play Pokemon Red, Blue and Yellow -- and Gold, in beta -- in 3D natively on TrimUI handhelds using Gen1Recomp 0.1.98 and the Dramaless Shape voxel 3D mod. Needs your own US cartridge dump.
paks.author: Carroarmato0

changelog.v0.1.0: Initial release, bundles Gen1Recomp 0.1.77 and the LOVE 11.5 aarch64 runtime.
changelog.v0.2.0: Now a Tool pak: it appears under Tools instead of Games, so no ROM folder or launchable stub file is needed. The automatic ROM import now finds your dump in any folder NextUI treats as Game Boy or Game Boy Color, not just the two default folder names, and says so in the log when it finds no such folder. Upgrading from v0.1.0: the first launch deletes the now-pointless Roms/Gen1Recomp (Gen1Recomp) folder, including any box art you put in it; delete Emus/<platform>/Gen1Recomp.pak yourself to reclaim ~31 MB. Your saves are untouched -- they live in .userdata/shared/Gen1Recomp.
changelog.v0.2.1: Fixes Pokemon Yellow. Two separate bugs stopped it working. First, the ROM scan gave up as soon as any one version had been imported, so a Yellow dump added after Red or Blue was never picked up -- the scan now tracks each version on its own, imports what is missing, leaves what is already there alone, and only stops once all three are in. Second, the game data Yellow needs to import was missing from the pak, so importing it failed with "ROM import metadata is missing"; it is now included. If you already have Red or Blue and a Yellow dump on your card, just launch the pak: it imports Yellow on the next start. Your saves are untouched.
changelog.v0.2.2: Fixes a crash that stopped the game starting at all on some devices. LOVE needs libmpg123, and not every TrimUI firmware image ships it -- where it was missing the game exited instantly to a black screen with "error while loading shared libraries: libmpg123.so.0". The pak now carries its own copy as a fallback, used only when the firmware has none. Thanks to @nicdichiara for finding and fixing this. Also: the pak now takes the game itself from upstream own build rather than a repackaged one, which is what caused Pokemon Yellow to be missing the data it needed to import, and refreshes the bundled certificate list. Your saves and imported ROMs are untouched.
changelog.v0.3.0: Adds Pokemon Gold, which upstream ships as a beta. Drop a US Gold dump in your Game Boy Color folder and the next launch imports it, the same as the others -- Gold is a 2 MB cartridge and the ROM scan now accepts that size, having previously skipped anything that was not exactly 1 MB. The launcher labels it Gold (Beta), so treat it as unfinished: it is Generation 2 and still being worked on upstream. Red, Blue and Yellow are unaffected. Updated to Gen1Recomp 0.1.81, which is mostly Gold fixes plus wrong-warp, encounter-rate and battle corrections. Your saves and imported ROMs are untouched.
changelog.v0.4.0: Swaps the bundled 3D voxel mod. The Dramatic Shape mod this pak shipped until now does not permit redistribution -- its author pulled the repository and its README forbids it -- so it has been replaced by Dramaless Shape 2.0.1, a community fork that rebased onto the last openly licensed version and ships under the MIT licence. The download drops from 39 MB to 22 MB. The new mod is built for weaker hardware -- it renders the 3D world at half resolution by default and adds a render-distance setting -- but be aware that it does not use less memory: measured on a Smart Pro S it peaks at 726 MB against the old mod's 722 MB, so Swap.pak is still required for 3D. It does less, though -- gone are the Pokemon Stadium battle models, the 3D battle modes, VR, and voxel character models, so people in the overworld are now flat sprites rather than 3D figures. If you preferred the old mod you can still install it yourself from the in-game mod manager. Note that the new mod's keyboard shortcuts do not work on a handheld, so switch the 3D view from the OPTIONS menu rather than with SELECT. Updating removes the old mod automatically; leaving it in place would have stopped the new one loading. New installs also get the official mod catalogue added to Find mods, so you can browse the other hundred-odd mods without typing a URL; remove it in-game if you would rather not, and it stays removed. Note that browsing that catalogue can freeze the game for up to a minute at a time -- the engine fetches over the network on the drawing thread, so the picture stops until the request finishes. It is not a crash; wait it out. One more thing worth knowing if you own several dumps: picking a version on the Choose ROM screen imports whichever edition has not been imported yet, which is not always the one you picked. Nothing is mislabelled, and everything you own imports over a few launches. Your saves and imported ROMs are untouched.
changelog.v0.4.1: Updates the game engine to Gen1Recomp 0.1.98, seventeen upstream releases on from the 0.1.81 this pak shipped before. That brings a long run of fixes to Red, Blue and Yellow -- the intro softlock, missing messages in Oak's lab and at the PC, the sell menu, selling TMs at marts, text speed and animation timing, several missing Pikachu interactions in Yellow -- and a batch of Gold fixes including Pokedex area data, Swift ignoring accuracy, Substitute's sprite and poison damage applying twice. Gold is still a beta upstream. Mods now run in a sandbox: upstream closed a hole where a mod could read and write files anywhere in your home directory, so mods no longer get the raw filesystem. The bundled Dramaless Shape voxel mod runs through the compatibility layer that ships with the sandbox, and its optional log-export button, which shelled out to another program, is refused under the new rules. Browsing the mod catalogue can still freeze the picture for up to a minute at a time -- that one is still open upstream, and still not a crash. Your saves and imported ROMs are untouched.

experimental_paks.description: Your whole RomM library on-device: games download when you launch them, saves and save states sync between all your devices
experimental_paks.author: lodordev

changelog.0.9.6: Self-update notices (store badge + daily check after a good sync), pairing self-heal for preseeded/cloned cards, Tailscale QR sign-in no longer times out, sync engine 0.9.6 (save-integrity + cross-device Recently Played interop).
changelog.0.9.7: 0.9.7: fleet core alignment (states-portable cores), stale auto-state retirement on restore, Handoff state manifests (dark), engine sync fixes. First release in lockstep with the new Android lane.
changelog.0.9.7.10: Stability release: multi-disc playlist fixes (CRLF/comments), resumable disc downloads, sync-collision honesty, durable settings writes.
changelog.0.9.7.11: Multi-disc hotfix: games launch after the first disc again (playlist tracks on-card discs; part-downloads migrate automatically); B actually cancels downloads; Miyoo Mini update screens fixed.
changelog.0.9.7.2: 0.9.7.2 — Handoff save-state core alignment (SNES/GBA/etc. now declare the real cores), save-state data-loss fixes, self-update honesty
changelog.0.9.7.3: 0.9.7.3 — Handoff save-state sync end-to-end: Sync Now + daemon now push save-states, on-exit state push decoupled from battery saves, offline queue/drain
changelog.0.9.7.4: 0.9.7.4 — Sync Now now pushes save-states (wired into the real sync paths), on top of the on-exit + offline-queue state sync
changelog.0.9.7.5: 0.9.7.5 — parity/maintenance. Adds an uninstall cleanup hook (post_uninstall) that clears saved server credentials on removal; activates once the pak store runs uninstall hooks. Picks up the current sync engine. No user-facing behavior change on NextUI.
changelog.0.9.7.6: 0.9.7.6 — Uninstall now clears your saved server credentials (config moved into the pak so removal wipes the RomM token; update_ignore preserves pairing across updates). Reinstall re-pairs. Plus engine reliability + security hardening.
changelog.0.9.7.7: Save states and saves sync more honestly: deleted saves stay deleted (newer progress from other devices still arrives), downloads resume after interruptions, library refresh shows live progress, errors wait to be read and name the real cause, and setup opens with a proper welcome page.
changelog.0.9.7.8: Fix release: update and Reset-WiFi screens no longer black out on Miyoo Mini devices, and downloaded updates now always install at reboot (older cards had a missing boot hook — now self-repairing).
changelog.0.9.7.9: Multi-disc games now start after downloading just one disc — the rest arrive in the background while charging. Self-signed HTTPS servers can onboard with an honest certificate prompt.
changelog.0.9.8: Sync you can see, updates you can trust: last-synced status on every screen, B stops long operations honestly, update downloads resume and can be reverted, consistent menu names.
changelog.0.9.8.1: Multi-disc games now show one launchable entry instead of two (the disc folder is hidden); part-downloaded games migrate automatically.
changelog.1.0.0-alpha1: First public alpha of the 1.0 line. Launch card on every device, GBA moves to mGBA fleet-wide, save + save-state sync hardened (downloaded saves are now verified against the server content hash before they touch the card), and the UX sweep lands: your NextUI font and wallpaper are inherited on every screen, cover art behind Game Manager and Search. Early on purpose - expect rough edges and report them.
